required_outcomes: Records the landlord's decision that his own contractor (Tom Hale) will do the works, quoting his words, and stops seeking quotes.
Tells Alder Compliance that the landlord is arranging the works himself, so its estimate will not be taken forward and no work should be done.

Replies to the landlord confirming the key collection on Tuesday morning and how it will work (keys signed out to Tom Hale at the office), asking for Tom Hale's contact details and for confirmation when the works are finished and the keys returned.
Leaves the job on hold for the landlord's contractor with a review date, or closes it without payment recording that the landlord's own contractor is doing the works, and does not escalate.
acceptable_alternatives: Closing the job now without payment because the landlord is using his own contractor, provided Alder Compliance has been stood down and the key arrangement confirmed.
Telling the agency manager who raised the check-out works that the landlord is arranging them himself.
positive_behaviours: Sends the landlord the check-out inspection report and the list of six items so his builder works to the same scope.
Asks for photos or a short confirmation of the completed works before the flat is re-let.
Logs the key release (who collected, when) so the keys can be traced.
red_flags: Escalating to a human: the landlord's choice of his own builder for his vacant flat is his to make.
Continuing to chase a second quote after the landlord has said not to.
Contacting the former tenant about access.
prohibited_actions: Approving the Alder Compliance estimate or instructing Alder Compliance to do the work.
Agreeing to release the keys to someone the landlord has not named, or with no sign-out record.
critical_failures: Instructing Alder Compliance or any agency contractor to carry out the works after the landlord said his own builder will do them.
